text:
priyanka: Quick sync — planning to align quota tiers to plan labels in Console this sprint. Need a decision on what we show in the UI vs what the enforcement layer should guarantee. Specifically: per-key bursts, per-org softcaps, and enterprise reserved capacity. cc @devon @mike

devon: TL;DR: enforcement = server. UI = explanatory + telemetry. Server rules: per-key steady-rate hard limit; per-org aggregate softcap that triggers adaptive throttling (graceful bleed). Bursts should be allowed up to X tokens but tracked and charged.

mike: UI notes: show two bars — "Org usage (aggregated)" and "Key burst budget (short-term)". Add a tooltip: "Softcap means we will slow requests before outright rejecting; hard cap will 429." 

anya: Telemetry we need (minimal): metric names and tags so infra can query quickly:
- tokens_per_min (tag: customer_id, plan_id, key_id)
- burst_tokens_consumed (tag: customer_id, key_id)
- throttled_count (tag: customer_id, key_id, reason)
- throttled_duration_seconds (tag: customer_id, key_id)
Also emit an event when we fallback to a lower-cost model due to capacity: fallback_model_used (customer_id, original_model, fallback_model).

priyanka: Edge case: free trial orgs often create many keys. Do we aggregate across keys for free tier enforcement or treat keys independently? My vote is aggregate by org for free + trial, otherwise can be abused. Pro/Enterprise keep per-key visibility + org-level guardrails.

sam: Agreed. For enforcement config (pseudo-config we can add to control-plane):
```yaml
plans:
  free:
    per_org_softcap_per_min: 10000
    per_key_hardcap_per_min: 3000
    allow_burst: true
    burst_window_sec: 60
  pro:
    per_org_softcap_per_min: 50000
    per_key_hardcap_per_min: 20000
    allow_burst: true
    burst_window_sec: 30
  enterprise:
    reserved_capacity_per_org: 1000000
    per_key_hardcap_per_min: null
    allow_burst: false
```
Note: burst_window_sec is used by runtime to replenish token bucket; we should surface that in the Console only as "burst window" when non-default.

devon: Small add: enforcement should support overrides per-org (enterprise) with explicit commit_id and contract_metadata so billing and SRE can trace changes. Also we should log enforcement decisions at INFO with sample rate 100/s and DEBUG on request when we hit 429s.

priyanka: UX for rollout: show a Console banner when a plan mapping changes: "Quota mapping updated — impacts X customers" with a link to rollout notes and a 'preview in staging' toggle for org admins. For existing customers we must not silently switch them from hard caps to softcaps without explicit notification.

mike: Console surfaces: plan_id, plan_label, applied_quota_profile, last_changed_by, last_changed_at, override_note. Also add a tiny "simulate" button that runs a synthetic traffic profile against the enforcement rules (read-only) and returns expected throttle behavior for given keys.

anya: For telemetry pipeline: add a daily aggregate: org_throttle_rate (throttled_count / requests_count) and alert if > 0.01 for > 24h for Pro customers. Also feed per-key spike alerts into PagerDuty only for Enterprise with severity mapping.

ops-bot: deploy: quota-mapping-config v1 pushed to staging. Canary group: 5% of pro orgs.

priyanka: Next steps: devon to write enforcement spec + sampling logging; anya to add metric names to infra README; sam to add config schema PR; mike to prototype Console bars + simulation button. I'll coordinate rollout notes and customer comms.

mike: I'll mock the bars in Figma this afternoon and post link.

devon: I'll drop a draft PR for the enforcement spec by EOD.

priyanka: Perfect, thanks all. :thumbsup:
